title: Can LLMs Write Backdoors? An Empirical Security Study of Weight-Space Programming
read_level: full (PDF via pdftotext; some table cells garbled in extraction, values taken from running text)
why_wsp: General-purpose LLMs receive a trained model's weights plus a natural-language backdoor spec and return modified weights, with no task data, no target forward passes and no gradients.
domain: backdoor injection into image classifiers (MNIST, CIFAR-10) and an LLM news classifier (AG News)
editor: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi-V3, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Tencent Hy4
target: MLP on MNIST; ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 (~11.18M params); Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct on AG News (base, full-FT, LoRA-FT variants)
interface: other (editor given weights; algorithm unprescribed; may inspect vocabulary or public references; no execution of target)
loop: one-shot (no feedback: "the independent evaluation results are not fed back to the editor")
self_editing: no; editors modify separate target models
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "only six parameters for the MLP and 0.02% of the weights for a fine-tuned Qwen model" (Abstract); ResNet-18 Astra edit "changed 83,407 scalar parameters (0.75% of the target model)" (Sec 4.2); Qwen Astra edit "changing 119,300 scalar parameters" (Sec 4.3)

headline_results.claim: Astra 100% ASR on all three targets
headline_results.quote: GPT-6 Astra achieves a 100% attack success rate across all three target models

headline_results.claim: MLP: 6 parameters, no measured clean-acc loss
headline_results.quote: Astra’s edit attained 100.00% Post-ASR while changing only six scalar parameters (Table 2). Clean accuracy remained at 94.99%, and FPR at 0.61%
Astra’s edited model reached 100.00% PostASR; clean accuracy decreased by 1.43 percentage points to 90.53%, and FPR increased from 1.11% to 1.76%
Full-Clean-Edit retained higher clean accuracy than Full-Poison (94.50% versus 94.02%) and a lower FPR (0.95% versus 1.25%)
GPT-5.6 Sol, Kimi-V3, and Tencent Hy4 obtained Post-ASR values of 0.88%, 0.94%, and 0.99%, respectively ... DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash reached 3.45% PostASR

headline_results.claim: All five editors backdoored the MLP with differing edit sizes
headline_results.quote: GPT-6 Astra modified 6 parameters, GPT-5.6 Sol 913, Kimi-V3 1,052, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 8,475, and Tencent Hy4 1,179
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash changed the fewest parameters among the successful ResNet-18 edits (29,769) but had the largest observed collateral effects: Clean ACC fell to 69.47% and FPR rose to 24.41%

cost.claim: No editor compute reported; training baselines' GPU memory only
cost.quote: These observations support a comparison of behavioral outcomes and weight changes, not a controlled claim of lower total compute cost

baselines_and_controls: Poisoning-based fine-tuning (full and LoRA for Qwen; 5% poisoned for MNIST/CIFAR); pre-edit ASR and FPR of starting models; cross-editor comparison under matched permissions.
runs_and_variance: single run / not reported; "our results characterize the available edited models rather than the success probability of individual editing requests, as complete editing-attempt records are not available" (Sec 5)
memorization_vs_reasoning: Editors could consult public reference materials (vision targets). RQ3 examines a Sol editing record (position-dependent trigger hypothesis) and DeepSeek weight diffs but states these "do not, by themselves, establish trigger-specific causation".
limitations_stated: Three architectures and specific triggers only; no per-request success probabilities (incomplete attempt records); exploratory analysis not causal.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (blog, Nov 2026)
Zeng et al., Lazare, veni foras (Microsoft Research preprint, Nov 2026)
notes_for_survey: Open-loop, data-free, no-forward-pass backdoor implantation by five LLM editors; capability differs sharply by editor (only Astra succeeded on Qwen). Results are from single returned models per editor-target, with no repeated attempts or robustness/detection tests.
